trimmed_dict.title: INPP Seminar - Hsin-Yu Chen (University of Texas at Austin)
trimmed_dict.date: Tuesday, April 21, 2026 4pm to 5pm
trimmed_dict.description:
From Heavy Elements to Dense Matter: Multimessenger Insights into Neutron Star Nuclear Physics 

 

 

Gravitational-wave detections of binary neutron star and neutron star–black hole mergers, together with their electromagnetic counterpart observations, offer powerful tools for exploring key questions in nuclear astrophysics. Different observational channels offer complementary insights and highlight the strength of multimessenger astronomy. In this talk, I will present how we combine gravitational-wave observations from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA with data from short and long gamma-ray bursts, Galactic pulsars, and stellar abundance measurements of [Eu/Fe] versus [Fe/H] to (i) evaluate the contribution of compact object mergers to r-process enrichment in the Galactic disk, and (ii) constrain the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff mass of neutron stars.
